summary: Payette NF lookout near McCall: camp 1913, 1916 pole tower, present 20-ft L-4 tower built 1955; NHLR-registered 2020 and staffed in season, though one FS guide says unmanned.

facts.design: Present 20-foot treated timber L-4 tower (built 1955); earlier 10-foot pole tower with 12 by 12 ft cab (1916); site a camp from 1913

staffing.status: staffed in fire season (NHLR; firelookout.com says every summer); one FS guide calls it unmanned

access.note: Hike-in via Trail #165 (non-motorized); sources do not describe rules for entering the tower itself

visit.trail_note: About 2.5 miles, climbing just under 2,000 ft, from Granite Mountain Trailhead off Goose Lake Road about 12.5 miles north of Highway 55. Trail page lists the New Meadows office as temporarily closed until further notice.

corrections.why: The present tower is a 20-foot treated timber L-4 tower (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts, firelookout.com), about 6.1 m. No source gives 3.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give three dates because they describe different stages on the site: a camp from 1913, a 10-foot pole tower with 12x12 cab in 1916, and the present 20-foot L-4 tower in 1955. The record's 1955 built date refers to the present tower and is kept.

NHLR says staffed every fire season and firelookout.com says every summer. A July 2025 Idaho visit found the tower staffed. An undated FS recreation guide says unmanned. The story reports the 2025 visit and the guide's wording and does not settle which is current.
The recreation guide names the McCall Ranger District, while the trail page's office contact is the New Meadows Ranger District. Both are reported; neither is changed in the record.
NHLR gives 8,478 ft (2,584 m), matching the record's 2584.1 m. The trail page gives about 8,480 ft and the recreation guide 8,470 ft as the end point. No change proposed.

notes_for_editor: Record height 3.7 m is wrong; the present tower is 20 ft (proposed 6.1 m). Name collision risk: two other Idaho lookouts are called Granite Mountain (Idaho Fire Lookouts southern-idaho page: 1923 camp, 2003 NHLR, North Fork Ranger District; north-idaho-panhandle-region page: 1932 cabin and 1934 L-4 tower, destroyed in the 1950s). Neither is this Payette tower and their facts were not merged. Current staffing is unverified for 2026: the staff list shows a 2026 entry and the 2025 visit confirmed a staffed season, but the FS guide (undated in the copy read) says unmanned. Staff names were deliberately left out of the research file; the staff list includes current seasonal staff. Access: the trail is public and non-motorized; no source describes rules for entering the tower. The NHLR page shows photos (1953 USFS, 2017 courtesy Keith Lanom) but no image URLs were retrieved, so no photos are recorded.
